des_teaser.label: Teaser — empty arena at 0:02

content.prompt: Cinematic wide-angle photograph of a dimly lit NBA basketball arena late at night. A single spotlight illuminates the court's three-point line near the hoop. An official NBA referee's whistle rests on the polished hardwood floor. The scoreboard in the distance reads 0:02. Mood: solemn, investigative, forensic. Deep navy shadows, amber spotlight, film grain.

des_teaser.brief: Full-viewport teaser: an empty arena at 0:02, a whistle on the floor, a single amber spotlight. No headline visible yet — the teaser is pure atmosphere. The scoreboard '0:02' establishes the L2M window without naming it.
des_teaser.rationale: An image teaser — not video — because the stillness is the point. The L2M is the moment after the action stops and the accounting begins.

des_01.label: Overall CC/CNC/IC/INC breakdown chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows exact count and percentage

style.palette: green for correct (CC/CNC shades), amber for IC, coral/red for INC

des_01.brief: A single horizontal stacked bar segmented into CC (29.58%), CNC (61.65%), IC (0.96%), INC (7.81%). Light greens for CC/CNC, amber for IC, coral for INC. Each segment labeled with percentage and absolute count. Hover tooltip gives full counts. The INC segment should subtly pulse or glow to foreshadow the 8:1 asymmetry discussed in edt_02. Width 100%, max 720px.
des_01.rationale: A stacked bar makes the proportions visceral: 91% correct is visible at a glance, but so is the 8% missed-call strip that sets up the next section.

des_01_stat.label: 91.23% correct stat callout

content.label: of late-game calls the NBA says it got right, across 25,057 reviewed decisions

des_01_stat.brief: Large 72px stat, amber-on-navy, centered. Underneath in smaller text: the denominator. Establishes the top-line number before the stacked bar breakdown.
des_01_stat.rationale: The headline number deserves its own moment before the chart dissects it.

des_hook_img.label: Hook image — game report on desk

content.prompt: Editorial photograph of an NBA official game report document on a wooden desk with a silver whistle, reading lamp, moody amber-and-navy lighting, investigative journalism feel. No text readable, no logos.

des_hook_img.brief: Editorial still life — the document itself, as object. Sits between the intro paragraph and the chart, grounds the concept of 'a PDF posted in the morning' in something physical.
des_hook_img.rationale: Reinforces the L2M as artifact, not abstraction.

des_02.label: Call-type error rate sorted bar chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows IC count, INC count, total plays. Click on bar expands a row explaining what that call is.

style.palette: coral gradient from dark (high error) to light (low error)

des_02.brief: Horizontal bars, sorted by error_pct descending. Defensive 3-second sits at the top at 63.6% — the bar should visually dominate. The last two bars (personal fouls at 5.4%, shooting at 7.0%) should feel small. Hover reveals the IC/INC split and total volume. The contrast between the high-rate exotic violations and the low-rate common fouls is the story.
des_02.rationale: Sorted bar chart is the clearest way to show that error rate is NOT uniform by call type. The cliff from the top three to the rest is the payoff.

des_02_stat.label: 63.6% missed defensive 3-seconds callout

content.label: of defensive 3-second violations are missed in the last two minutes

des_02_stat.brief: Large 72px stat beside or above the sorted bar chart. The number that should make the reader stop reading and reread. Coral accent.
des_02_stat.rationale: The single most surprising number in the dataset — deserves callout treatment.

des_03.label: Errors-per-game distribution chart

content.color: errors_in_game (step gradient — light for 0, dark for 5+)
content.interaction: hover tooltip shows 'N games ended with X errors' and percentage of dataset

des_03.brief: Simple vertical bar chart. X = number of errors (0, 1, 2, ... 14), Y = count of games with that many errors. Bars at 0, 1, 2 should be tall (426, 427, 336). Tail from 5+ should be short and pointed — including the singleton 14-error bar, which should be coral-red. Annotate the mean (1.49) as a vertical dashed line.
des_03.rationale: A distribution chart makes the 'most games have 0-2 errors, a rare few have many' pattern obvious.

des_04.label: Season trend line chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows all four numbers (games, total_plays, error_pct, errors_per_game) for the season

style.palette: coral for error rate, navy for per-game count

des_04.brief: Line chart across 4 seasons. Primary line: error_pct descending from 13.03 to 6.15, coral color with area fill under it. Secondary line: errors_per_game, navy, descending from 1.84 to 1.27. Annotate 2014-15 as '(partial season)' and 2017-18 as '(scope expanded)'. The visual pattern of both lines falling together is the point.
des_04.rationale: A line chart with two converging falling trends shows both that error rates dropped AND per-game counts dropped — ruling out 'they just review more now so the rate went down' as the sole explanation.

des_04_stat.label: Halved in three years
des_04_stat.brief: Large arrow-style stat, with the before→after numbers in coral. Short caption underneath.
des_04_stat.rationale: Makes the trend a single memorable visual.

des_05.label: Scott Foster positioning vs league

content.color: highlight Scott Foster in coral, others grey
content.interaction: hover tooltip shows games, plays, IC, INC, error_pct for each ref

style.palette: grey dots for most refs, coral dot for Scott Foster
style.reference_line: vertical dashed line at league median (8.83%)

des_05.brief: A dot plot of the 15 most-worked referees, sorted by error_pct. Each ref is a horizontal row with their name and a dot at their error percentage. Scott Foster's dot is coral; the rest are muted grey. A vertical dashed line marks the league median (8.83%). Label above Foster: '49th of 59 — below median, not an outlier.' The visual lets the reader see Foster's position in context in one glance.
des_05.rationale: Placing Foster in context of his peers is the whole argument of the section. A dot plot does this without misleading bar comparisons.

des_05_img.label: Referee silhouette

content.prompt: NBA referee in black-and-white vertical-striped uniform, back to camera, standing on a professional basketball court mid-game. No visible face. Editorial sports photography.

des_05_img.brief: Image of a referee from behind — the figure we're all blaming, but anonymous. Opens the Foster section before the name lands.
des_05_img.rationale: Lets the reader sit with 'the referee' as an archetype before the individual name enters the story.

des_06.label: Best-vs-worst referees ranked

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows games and plays for each ref

style.palette: teal for bottom-10 (best), coral for top-10 (worst)
style.annotations: Worst: Tre Maddox 11.00% | Best: Dedric Taylor 6.58% | Spread: 4.42 pts

des_06.brief: A twin-column horizontal bar chart — left: 10 worst refs in coral (ascending by error_pct), right: 10 best in teal (descending). Gap in the middle labeled 'league median 8.83%'. Shows the full spread at a glance. Every bar labeled with exact percentage.
des_06.rationale: Juxtaposing best and worst makes the spread feel physical. The gap in the middle is where most refs actually sit.

des_07.label: Home vs away disadvantage pie/donut + hunk comparison

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows exact counts and percentages

style.palette: teal for home, coral for away

des_07.brief: Three horizontal bars — IC errors, INC errors, combined. Each bar stacked with home-team-hurt (teal) and away-team-hurt (coral) portions. The 'combined' bar should look almost symmetric (49.88/50.12). The IC bar shows the minor lean to home-hurt (52.89/47.11). Label each bar with exact pct. The visual payoff: the bars look much more equal than the fan would expect.
des_07.rationale: Reveals the non-result — the lean is tiny. The side-by-side view makes it obvious the 'home bias' story collapses under this data.

des_08.label: Player net-disadvantage chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows total_appearances, disadvantaged_by_err, committed_err, net

style.palette: coral for hurt players (positive net), teal for advantaged players (negative net)

des_08.brief: Horizontal bidirectional bar chart. Top half: 15 most-hurt players (Wiggins +15 at top, coral bars). Bottom half: 15 most-advantaged players (Gortat -38 at bottom, teal bars). Zero line down the middle. Annotate Wiggins and Gortat with their stats. Also annotate LeBron James near zero with 'LeBron: -5' to underline the near-neutrality. Hover tooltip reveals the asymmetry: X times hurt vs Y times fouled.
des_08.rationale: A bidirectional bar is the clearest way to show both populations in one chart. The visual symmetry between the top and bottom halves is the dramatic payoff.

des_08_img.label: Drive to the rim image

content.prompt: Dramatic sports photograph of a blurred NBA player mid-drive to the rim with motion blur. Defender's arm in foreground. Mid-collision ambiguity. No faces, no logos.

des_08_img.brief: Visual beat about the guard driving into contact — the kind of play that produces the hardest-to-judge calls. Appears before the chart to prime the reader visually.
des_08_img.rationale: Grounds the 'guards get hurt, bigs get charged' thesis in the actual on-court action the data summarizes.

des_09.label: Error rate by seconds-left chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows exact percentages and counts

style.palette: navy bars for volume, coral line for error rate

des_09.brief: X axis: 0-9s on the right, 110-119s on the left (time flows toward buzzer). Navy bars: volume of reviewed decisions (showing the spike in last 30 seconds). Overlay coral line: error_pct, which dips to 6.62% at 0-9s. The visual dissonance (most calls, fewest errors) is the point.
des_09.rationale: Combining volume and error rate on the same time axis shows that the densest stretch is also the most accurate — the exact opposite of what the reader expects.

des_10_img.label: Closing image — empty arena at 0:00

content.prompt: Cinematic photograph of an empty NBA arena from the upper bowl. Scoreboard shows '0:00'. Dimmed stadium lights, warm accent lighting. No players, no people.

des_10_img.brief: Closing image — the arena after the game is over, scoreboard reading 0:00. Mirrors the 0:02 of the teaser. Quiet, conclusive.
des_10_img.rationale: Book-ends the narrative — the teaser opened with 0:02 still on the clock; the close shows the clock at zero, the decision reviewable.

page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-then-chart, with full-width atmospheric images breaking up the chart flow every 2-3 sections
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Body text in Georgia/system-serif. Stats and section titles in system-ui/sans-serif. Large callouts at 72px. Section dividers use thin horizontal lines with navy-coral gradient. Navy (#0f172a) for background or accents, coral (#e94e4e) for highlighted data, teal (#14b8a6) for 'good' / positive framings, amber for neutral accents.
